items.summary: Over 50 AI agent experiments saved 1,257 gzip bytes for every website loading Clarity. Why a bigger 2,308-byte saving was held back to protect Angular apps.

items.title: Shakira loses YouTube's No. 1 to LISA for the second time in seven weeks
items.summary: Tarantino drew 71.7M views and led the US, UK, German, Dutch and Australian charts. LISA's last No. 1 lost 79% of its views in week two. Will this one hold?

items.title: Google faces refiled Gemini Gmail suit after judge found no concrete harm
items.summary: Gmail, Chat and Meet users say Google enabled AI smart features without consent in fall 2025. Its second dismissal bid asks one thing: where is the actual harm?

items.title: Publisher group says AI cut visitors 26%, quoting Microsoft's 'doom loop'
items.summary: Referral traffic to surveyed publishers fell a median 22% over eight weeks in 2026, after a 10% drop in 2025. Will Judge Stein accept the brief and its data?

items.title: Advertisers in 10 more countries can't opt out of Google's AI Mode ads
items.summary: Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns in India, Kenya and 8 more markets now enter AI Mode. Brazil and Mexico, due in Q4, test the English-only list.

items.title: Microsoft lets advertisers set up to 40 guidelines for AI-written ads
items.summary: Conversions API leaves its per-account pilot with 10 named partners, and Performance Max adds search term reports. Landing page data follows from mid-November.

items.title: Microsoft Audience ads gain option to show only to chosen LinkedIn job roles
items.summary: Search, Shopping and Dynamic Search Ads campaigns stay bid-only for B2B advertisers using LinkedIn data. Which limits still apply to company lists and reach?

items.title: Google Search product panels gain Add to cart and Buy now buttons
items.summary: Retailers' Visit site link stays on top, yet a code cut a $70 case to $59.50 inside Google's panel. Saved carts stay invisible to shops. Who gets the credit?

items.title: Google AI Mode test groups shopping ads under one Sponsored heading
items.summary: Retailers' unpaid listings get an "All products" heading in the test, spotted October 28 by Search Engine Watch. Will one label per group change the clicks?

items.title: Google Search ad gains Apple Messages button that sends iPhone users to SMS
items.summary: Philadelphia injury firm's ad pre-filled a text to its toll-free line. Google's iOS list of 42 countries omits the US. A test, or the SMS asset in Apple's name?

items.title: Google Gemini drops UTM tags from cited links after three weeks
items.summary: Tagged Gemini visits peaked at 83 a day in one consultant's logs before falling to 3. Visits arriving with no referrer go back to Direct, and Google is silent.

items.title: Affle agrees to buy Perion for $420 million at a 34.5% premium
items.summary: Perion shareholders get $11.70 a share in cash; Perion held $228.3m in cash and securities on Sept 30. A go-shop runs to Dec 11 - will a higher bid surface?

items.title: Google, Microsoft & OpenAI Plan To Honor Shared AI Training Opt-Out via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.summary: A shared robots.txt line could let sites opt out of AI training with several providers at once, but companies involved are handling it differently. The post Google, Microsoft & OpenAI Plan To Honor Shared AI Training Opt-Out appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

Under the theme "Build, Secure, Scale," participants gain hands-on experience with Google’s developer stack—including Gemini, Google AI Studio, Google Antigravity, and Web MCP—through live workshops and codelabs. items.title: Build Generative UI Apps with A2UI & CopilotKit Agents
items.summary: See Google A2Ui in action! Learn how to natively render agentic UIs across Langchain, AWS Strands, Microsoft agents, and Google ADK using CopilotKit SDKs for A2UI.

items.title: Smaller apps and faster GPU inference with LiteRT in Google Play services
items.summary: LiteRT in Google Play services now offers GPU inference powered by ML Drift, delivering about 1.4x faster performance alongside the new CompiledModel API. Switching from bundled binaries reduces app size by approximately 8 MB while enabling seamless, automatic runtime updates across billions of devices. Developers can easily adopt these updates by updating their dependencies and utilizing the new Android Studio LiteRT skill for automated migration.

items.title: Hill-Climbing Agent Quality with Agents CLI Evaluation
items.summary: This post walks through the Agents CLI evaluation loop for systematically improving agent performance through continuous testing and grading. It demonstrates how to catch prompt regressions, evaluate model backend swaps using side-by-side trace comparisons, and automate evaluation passes. Developers will also learn how to integrate nightly scheduled runs with threshold-based alerting to track quality over time.

items.title: Building Conversational Commerce with Multi-Agent Swarms on GCP: A Working Prototype
items.summary: This document provides a publication template and metadata structure for a technical blog post focused on building Conversational User Interfaces (CUIs) using AI. It outlines key developer focus areas, product stacks, and approval workflows required for publishing technical content through Google Developer Studio. The framework helps engineers organize their guides and solutions to effectively share AI-driven conversational interface designs with the developer community.

items.title: Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats
items.summary: A2UI now supports swappable inference formats, introducing A2UI Express which uses up to 3x fewer tokens and cuts latency by compiling compact Python-style syntax into standard A2UI JSON via Agent SDKs. Developers can also use controlled generation with TypeSafe's Jev system-decision models to render known-shape screens in under 300 ms while smaller models stream text. items.title: Preview, edit, and collaborate on markdown (.md) files natively in Google Docs and Drive
items.summary: Google Workspace now offers native support for Markdown (.md) files, allowing developers and AI agents to seamlessly collaborate on documentation directly in Google Docs without manual file conversions. This integration preserves native file fidelity for use with Git repositories and developer tools while unlocking standard Docs features like line-level commenting, rendered Drive previews, and tracked version history.

items.title: Architecting Governed, Self-Evolving AI Agents on Google Cloud
items.summary: Learn how Project Chrysalis combines Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Development Kit (ADK), BigQuery, and a four-gate defense-in-depth security stack (Model Armor, Cloud KMS, Binary Authorization, and OPA) to build governed, self-evolving AI agents that remediate live production outages in 1.8 seconds.

items.title: Streaming comes to API Gateway: real-time and AI-ready APIs, without changing your spec
items.summary: API Gateway now supports real-time streaming—including Server-Sent Events, WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding—in Public Preview without requiring changes to your existing API specifications. This update allows developers to route long-lived, bi-directional streams and AI workloads directly through the gateway while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability. items.title: Powering the Agent Development Lifecycle with any framework, from ADK to LangChain and beyond
items.summary: The Agents CLI Extension System enables developers to use frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or custom enterprise stacks while retaining a unified deployment and evaluation workflow. It details a first-party LangChain template that scaffolds, runs, and deploys agents without requiring the Agent Development Kit (ADK). Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.

items.title: Unifying Edge AI: How Coral NPU’s open standard brings portable, energy-viable intelligence from model to silicon
items.summary: Google Research has completed the 32-bit open-source Coral NPU RISC-V architecture with the introduction of its Matrix Execution Unit, which delivers up to 1 TOPS while targeting 10 mW average power for edge inference. Alongside this architecture, the release of the v1.0 open-source IREE/MLIR compiler allows developers to take models from JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow straight to Coral NPU hardware without writing custom assembly. items.title: Bringing Visual Graph Debugging to Custom Edge Compilers with Model Explorer
items.summary: Google AI Edge Model Explorer now supports custom compiler intermediate representations and open-source adapters like TOSA, VGF, and PTE for on-device machine learning. Developers can leverage hierarchical graph visualization, split-pane views, and per-node trace overlays to catch export regressions and verify hardware delegation. These tools enable engineering teams to transparently debug execution graphs and pinpoint cycle-level latency bottlenecks locally.

items.title: Announcing New vLLM and SGLang Inference Engines on TPU
items.summary: This post announces native PyTorch backends for vLLM and SGLang powered by TorchTPU, enabling developers to run and optimize serving workloads using familiar PyTorch tools. Built in collaboration with open-source project maintainers, these engines include optimized TPU kernel implementations, production-ready features like KV cache management with TPU Sync, and disaggregated serving. items.summary: TorchTPU integrates a native torch.device("tpu") backend directly into PyTorch, allowing developers to train large-scale models on Google Cloud TPUs without rewriting code in JAX. The TorchTitan TPU fork enhances this with production-grade scaling primitives like SimpleFSDP, Graph Trainer, and custom Pallas kernels that achieve high Model Flops Utilization (MFU) across dense and MoE architectures. items.title: Step by Step guide: Build a Voice Agent That Never Goes Silent using ADK
items.summary: The open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) and gemini-3.8-live enable developers to build responsive voice agents by implementing non-blocking tools in Python. Developers can use streaming tools to yield progress updates or background execution patterns to keep conversations fluid during long-running backend queries. items.title: Native Model Authoring for Edge with LiteRT Tensor API
items.summary: Meet the LiteRT Tensor API: giving developers native C++ control over the model graph to unify end-to-end ML computations on heterogeneous edge hardware.

items.title: Three layers, one repo: a tour of google/adk-recipes
items.summary: The google/adk-recipes repository unifies Agent Development Kit (ADK) resources into three structured layers—core/, plugins/, and contrib/—serving as a single source of truth for building AI agents. Developers can leverage reference patterns, install modular vertical skills (such as retail product search and virtual try-on) directly into their coding assistants, and deploy production-ready services across multiple languages. items.title: Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
items.summary: A practical engineering guide and reference architecture for establishing continuous evaluation pipelines for multi-turn AI agents using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google ADK, and OpenInference standards.

items.title: Announcing DPoP Support for Google OAuth: Securing Refresh Tokens
items.summary: Google OAuth Platform now supports DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession) to sender-constrain refresh tokens, neutralizing Infostealer malware and adversary-in-the-middle attacks. By cryptographically binding long-lived refresh tokens while maintaining short-lived access tokens as standard Bearer tokens, developers achieve robust credential security without incurring high-QPS API performance overhead.
